leo: quick flag - rolled a small eval of ranky-7b-q4h-v1 on holdout_sample and seeing a ~5% NDCG@10 regression concentrated on very short queries (<8 tokens).
anika: interesting, q4h is our hybrid 4-bit config right? Any change in preprocessing or candidate set?
leo: nothing changed upstream. run: `python rerank_eval.py --model ranky-7b-q4h-v1 --dataset holdout_sample --k 10 --slices short_queries,mid,long --seed 7 --out results_q4h.json`
jas: does MRR move the same way?
leo: MRR ~ -1.1%, P@1 -2.8. It's mostly top-1 churn on terse queries like "scp windows to mac".
toni: could be per-head quantization artifacts - we've seen head-wise scale mismatch compressing final logits before softmax. Any per-layer scale logs?
leo: I dumped final layer scales for a few examples - last linear norm is smaller on q4h vs fp16 by ~0.4 std dev. Short queries show more compression.
anika: sounds like a dynamic range mismatch. Try per-layer rescale: multiply final linear output by 1.15 and recompute ranks to see if ordering recovers.
jas: also run a per-head dequant (reconstruct floats for last-attn heads) on a few flips to debug whether attention scores changed or the final MLP dominates.
leo: good call. I'll produce per-head attention score diffs and topk candidate traces. Adding `--emit-head-trace` to the eval harness.

ci-bot: nightly-eval job finished - no infra failures :white_check_mark:

leo: quick example from traces (short):
- query: "install node mac"
- baseline top1: docX (gap=2.3)
- q4h top1: docY (gap=0.1)
- per-head trace: head4 attention diff large, head11 tiny. overall final logit compressed.

toni: that pattern matches head-saturating quant. PTQ per-head clip might be too aggressive. What's our PTQ config (clip, per_channel)?
leo: ptq.yml snippet: `clip_value: 3.0, per_channel: false, calibration_samples: 512`
anika: try `per_channel: true` for q4h and increase clip to 6.0 for last linear only. Re-run a small subset to validate.
jas: while you're at it, compute correlation between doc token length and score delta. If short docs/queries are overrepresented we may have a length-dependent bias.
leo: running three quick experiments tonight: (A) per_channel true, clip 3.0; (B) per_channel true, clip 6.0 for last_linear; (C) apply post-quant affine rescale (scale=1.15) to final logits. I'll put outputs under s3://rerank-experiments/1764202468_q4h_headscale/

toni: if (C) recovers most of the signal we can ship a transient calibration transform in serving while PTQ is fixed. But we should also add a CI smoke: quantized build must pass a short-query NDCG probe within 2% of fp16.
anika: agreed. Also include a human review set (20 flips) with snippet diffs and tokenizer boundaries - short query subtokens can flip the attention distribution.
leo: noted. Example subtoken issue: q "scp windows to mac" tokenized -> ["sc", "p", " windows", " to", " mac"] causing odd alignments. Will attach tokenization for flip samples.
jas: add `--seed` sweep (3 seeds) to see if this is stochastic from calibration. Configure harness to emit per-query zscore: `--emit-score-deltas zscores.json`.

leo: interim result: experiment (C) affine scale 1.15 recovered ~3.8% of NDCG loss (net -1.2% vs fp16). per_channel true + clip 6.0 recovered ~4.6% (net -0.4%).

toni: nice. Sounds like per-channel clipping on last linear plus slight affine could be the fix. Open a PTQ ticket to update kernel and add per-layer clip whitelist.
anika: I'll draft the ticket. Also add a dashboard panel for short-query NDCG by build ID so we catch regressions early.
jas: and a small gating check in weekly release pipeline: run a 500-sample short-query probe for any quant candidate.

leo: will upload traces, human CSV and a short notebook with plots to the S3 path and open PR for CI probe.

ci-bot: PR check - rerank_eval harness tests passed 68/68 :party_parrot:

anika: thanks all. Ping when PTQ ticket is up and results are in S3.
leo: pinged :rocket:"
